reader.notes: OrdMin* return ExtremeIndex/SelectExact + 1 (1-based); the renderer flattens ALL subscripts within the current ODO bound. OrdMinReal (binary64 carrier) is unreachable from COBOL-85 source except through a real-valued function argument; it shares the kernel. Observation (not a conformance defect): CobolIntrinsics.ExactValue.cs#SelectExact re-writes the leftmost-strict-update loop beside the unified ExtremeIndex kernel (PB2635 unified the other carriers); the exact lane is what native ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN/MAX/MIN take.

refuter.evidence: Code: SelectExact (ExactValue.cs:32-42) and ExtremeIndex (Selection.cs:35-45) both start at index 0 and move only on a strict order (c<0 / c>0), so the leftmost of equal values is kept; ORD-* add 1.
